## Editor's Brief

The past 24 hours have seen a dramatic escalation between the United States and Iran, with both sides launching direct strikes that shatter the fragile April ceasefire. Simultaneously, the war in Ukraine enters a new phase as Sweden pledges advanced fighter jets, while the Indo-Pacific reflects deepening arms competitions—Taiwan test-fires American drones, Japan fields hypersonic weapons, and the U.S. House unveils a trillion-dollar defense bill targeting China. Below are the key developments to track.

- **U.S.-Iran tit-for-tat escalates into open hostilities**: After blaming Tehran for downing an Apache helicopter, the U.S. struck southern Iran. Iran retaliated by launching [drone and missile attacks on the U.S. Fifth Fleet in Bahrain](https://news.google.) and other Persian Gulf assets, and the U.S. continued strikes into a second day. The ceasefire is effectively dead, and Israel braces for Iranian missile retaliation.
- **Ukraine war: Putin rejects talks, Sweden sends 16 Gripen jets**: Russian President [Putin refused Zelenskyy's negotiation offer](https://news.google.) as fighting intensifies. Sweden pledged [16 Saab Gripen jets with 200-km-range missiles](https://news.google.) to Ukraine, a significant capability boost that will force Russia to adjust its air-defense posture. Ukraine also conducted long-range strikes on military and energy sites inside Russia.
- **Taiwan tests American attack drones against maritime targets**: Taiwan’s newly acquired U.S.-made attack drones [struck offshore targets in live-fire drills](https://news.usni.org/2026/06/10/taiwanese-forces-deploy-american-made-attack-drones-against-maritime-targets) along the west coast, validating long-range strike systems designed to counter a potential Chinese invasion. The deployment marks a tactical shift toward unmanned systems in the Taiwan Strait.
- **Japan unveils hypersonic glide vehicle to counter China**: The Japan Self-Defense Forces now field the [25HGP hypersonic glide vehicle](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMilAFBVV95cUxQSUZIYndSZGhEQi0wUldfbll3eFRfRkVCRGk1WE5sZk03QXVZRXI4cUlVbGxtZ2t4LUN1X0JNTkFpSWY5bE5MSHB3MFBaTUtpZTJVblN1VzVtN2dKYWxnVzRtZ0kxR3BMVVNKRUFSYVQ1MDMySVNwV3NROTlPLXo3VXVNNzg5dFR4MThuU0tIQlhXaS03), described as an effective response to China’s growing missile arsenal. This is part of a regional arms race as East Asia invests in speed and payload.
- **U.S. House releases $1 trillion FY27 defense bill, targets China**: The House appropriators’ [FY27 defense bill](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMingFBVV95cUxNVnVYeEFqcnJYUVZZbk9JbmwyTUxuT3pFSlVDSVpENW5rS2VNSGRwcV9VcFl0alFqdUFDRVVOR3lHMm0zZjdYamdiei1xVDVKZmxwcFNPRUU2c0JuemNtanFmOGRfb0lGQUVMRUxGd09IRV95cFR5TkZ3YjRxOVVraHRrdnQ4bW9xcHFqNFloaFJKeXhZdTVueEFUUllrZw) prioritizes countering China and includes provisions to decouple supply chains. Separately, the U.S. expanded its Chinese military-company blacklist to include BYD and other firms, while the Czech Republic restricted Chinese vehicles from sensitive military areas.
- **Naval developments: BALTOPS begins, new U.S. sub revealed**: NATO’s [BALTOPS 2026 exercise](https://news.usni.org/2026/06/10/baltops-2026-exercise-begins) kicked off with fewer ships due to redeployments to the Middle East. New images emerged of the [USS District of Columbia (SSBN-826)](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/06/new-look-at-americas-next-ballistic-missile-submarine/), America’s next ballistic missile submarine. Japan and South Korea resumed a [search-and-rescue exercise](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/06/japan-and-south-korea-resume-sarex-after-nine-year-hiatus/) after a nine-year hiatus, signaling improved bilateral military coordination.
- **European defense realignment: Germany’s air show and FCAS uncertainty**: The [ILA Berlin air show](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/2026/06/10/german-air-show-opens-under-shadow-of-iran-war-fighter-project-collapse/) opened under the shadow of the Iran conflict and the potential collapse of the Franco-German-Spanish Future Combat Air System (FCAS) project, with Airbus now looking to Sweden’s Saab as a preferred partner.

**Watch next**: The U.S.-Iran spiral could trigger further regional escalation—watch for [Hormuz Strait disruptions](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiVEFVX3lxTFBDdTkwajBzNElvRko1OC01eWZiQkxlM05zU3g1c1ZPY0ZMczhaMkJaY1p1dUtNOGpKa1F0M2NaQnBMUGRYTGtCdXh2T2IzdTZBTEdvbg) and Israeli preemptive moves. The FCAS program’s fate will reshape European aerospace. Taiwan’s drone integration and Japan’s hypersonic work are signals of a broader shift to unmanned and high-speed warfare in the Indo-Pacific.

## 海军与印太 · 7 items

Naval dynamics in the Indo-Pacific and beyond are shifting: Taiwan tests attack drones against maritime targets, NATO’s BALTOPS proceeds with reduced forces, Japan and South Korea renew bilateral drills, and the U.S. pushes ahead with its next ballistic missile submarine.

- **Taiwanese forces strike maritime targets with U.S. attack drones**: During [live-fire drills](https://news.usni.org/2026/06/10/taiwanese-forces-deploy-american-made-attack-drones-against-maritime-targets), Taiwan’s newly acquired American drones hit offshore targets, demonstrating a key capability for anti-invasion operations. The exercise validates long-range strike concepts that would be critical in a Taiwan Strait crisis.
- **BALTOPS 2026 begins with fewer ships due to Middle East commitments**: NATO’s [Baltic Operations exercise](https://news.usni.org/2026/06/10/baltops-2026-exercise-begins) includes 20 ships and 6,000 personnel from 15 allies, down from 2025 because naval assets are diverted to the Middle East. For the first time since 1972, the exercise is commanded from JFC Brunssum, reflecting NATO’s evolving command structure.
- **New images of USS District of Columbia (SSBN-826) emerge**: Photos of the [next-generation ballistic missile submarine](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/06/new-look-at-americas-next-ballistic-missile-submarine/) show progress on the bow and stern sections, including the X-shaped rudder. The Columbia class is critical to maintaining U.S. strategic deterrence.
- **Japan and South Korea resume SAREX after nine-year hiatus**: The [Japan Maritime SDF and ROK Navy](https://www.navalnews.com/naval-news/2026/06/japan-and-south-korea-resume-sarex-after-nine-year-hiatus/) conducted a search-and-rescue exercise west of Japan’s Goto Islands on June 7. This thaw in military cooperation is significant given historical tensions and shared security concerns over North Korea and China.
- **Fatal shooting aboard USS John F. Kennedy (CVN-79)**: Two sailors involved in the [shooting](https://news.usni.org/2026/06/10/sailors-involved-in-jfk-shooting-were-part-of-carriers-in-port-security-force) were part of the carrier’s in-port security force. One sailor was killed; the other is in pretrial confinement. The incident raises questions about security protocols on new construction vessels.

**Signal**: The Indo-Pacific maritime domain is seeing intensified drills and capability demonstrations, even as NATO navies are stretched by Middle Eastern commitments. Taiwan’s drone integration is a bellwether for future littoral combat.

## 中国军情 · 10 items

China continues to face pressure from multiple directions: Japan’s criticism of its military activities, U.S. legislative and blacklist moves targeting Chinese defense and tech firms, and European restrictions on Chinese vehicles. Beijing is pushing back against what it calls ‘unfounded accusations’ while experts warn of rising tensions in the West Pacific.

- **Japan accuses China of ‘normal military activities’, Beijing rebuts**: The Chinese Foreign Ministry [rejected](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMicEFVX3lxTE9lXzV3dU8wbC1yNWtNQzVmaGRUNWYwem91bFhWWDgwWklRVVU5cVpwbWltTkNXUXJuQXhoMEI0Y0FUNGVGVF9ubHhCZmhxQ05UYUZOR282ajgyWDZWZE9KUmVpUVZWTURLRDRLb1VRMTE) Japanese claims that China’s military activities are destabilizing, describing them as unfounded and designed to deceive the public. This exchange underscores growing friction in East China Sea and Taiwan Strait monitoring.
- **U.S. House FY27 defense bill targets China**: The [bill](https://news.google.) names China the principal strategic competitor and includes provisions to decouple critical supply chains. It reinforces the bipartisan consensus in Washington to contain Beijing.
- **U.S. expands Chinese military-company blacklist**: [BYD, Unitree, and others](https://news.google.) were added to the Pentagon’s list of Chinese military companies. BYD quickly [rejected the designation](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiW0FVX3lxTE45VzVtQUhjbWZva3RlNVdLVXNlWWp0bUx5WDJnVW1EM3BTNEpfTEYyT0MwMWFTV25RbG1kbEsxRW9VU3lMcHJDUzRlM29qZmVsNGxoNEVzanlPeDQ) as baseless, highlighting the expanding scope of U.S. technology restrictions.
- **Czech Republic restricts Chinese cars near military zones**: The Czech Defense Ministry is [limiting Chinese-made vehicles](https://news.google.) from entering sensitive military areas, citing espionage risks. This follows a trend of European allies tightening restrictions on Chinese technology.
- **West Pacific ‘undercurrents’ analyzed by experts**: A Chinese [expert analysis](https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiiAFBVV95cUxNaUhPM2dlMXFGc2FSWkdncXFDa0E3UkF1dDVaSVBZT3I4X21PbHAxNDF3T19MRWU2b2NOVFBCNTBLMkVHR1BxVlQzcTlHVUhub0N5UXRVWXY3Rnd0U1VZSFlLS3Z6SDM1Tkt0eVdBRlFsWUtmcmd3Ni1PRkJnQ0F4Zk45UzBVM0pU) warns that tensions in the West Pacific are at a dangerous inflection point, with the U.S., Japan, and Taiwan all pressing aggressive military postures that China views as provocations.

**Signal**: The U.S. and its allies are systematically tightening the screws on China’s defense and tech sectors, while China seeks to frame its military activities as routine. Expect further friction as the FY27 bill moves through Congress and blacklists expand.
